text:
toni (infra): Quick heads-up — we've seen a rise in Xid 13 on the eu-west1 A10 pool over the last 24h, but it's pretty noisy. I'm going to run a randomized sample across cards to try to pinpoint flaky hardware.

maria (sre): saw the spike in grafana. started ~04:10 UTC. Any correlation to small-batch decodes or single-token latencies?

kevin (runtime): Preliminary traces: ~90% of the Xid13s are happening during decode kernels with batch_size<=2 and seq_len<=64. Low occupancy path looks suspicious.

toni (infra): Good. Plan: take ~5% of cards from each rack (randomized by job_hash) and run decode_fuzz for 30m. If a card exceeds threshold Xid_count -> softdrain and deeper mem/NIC checks.

rachel (platform): Heads-up: spare capacity in eu-west1 is tight this week (reserved commits). Softdrain will increase latency for some dedicated routes. Can we route only best-effort tenants off those cards?

toni (infra): Yes — add routing-tier=best-effort and set fallback to eu-central when available. Also enable extra NV logging on sampled machines: /var/log/nv/xid_dump.log

ops-bot: :warning: [alert] xid13-rate eu-west1-a10 pool increased 3.2x — creating ticket INF-4521 and paging infra-oncall.

kevin (runtime): Kicking off sampling job now. Command I'm using: 

```
./tools/decode_fuzz --cards $(cat sample_list.txt) --duration 1800 --batch_sizes 1,2 --seq 8,32,64 --log /var/log/nv/xid_dump.log
```

maria (sre): If we confirm faulty cards, I recommend NIC firmware refresh + run ECC memtest (memtest86 adapted for GPU). Last time NIC microbursts + old firmware produced transient Xid13s.

toni (infra): Agree. I'm also toggling nv_err_timeout=5s on the driver (experiment) to force faster soft timeouts and see if that reduces hard Xids. Will keep it reversible.

kevin (runtime): Update: within 12 mins the fuzz job hit 3 cards. Suspect IDs: gpu-evict-42, gpu-evict-57, gpu-evict-88. Small dump snippet below:

```
[2026-06-12T04:23:18Z] Xid 13 on gpu-evict-42 decode_kernel.c:0x1a3f
[2026-06-12T04:23:19Z] pci_dev 0000:3b:00.0 NIC: microburst detected, tx_queue_full
[2026-06-12T04:23:19Z] ECC: single-bit corrected at 0x7fffa2b00
[2026-06-12T04:23:20Z] driver nv: raising hard_error -> XID13
```

maria (sre): That's a useful pattern — NIC microburst record immediately preceding Xid13 + corrected ECC. Sounds like a transient IO burst causing kernel to escalate.

ton i (infra): Next steps proposed: 1) softdrain those 3 cards (route best-effort tenants away), 2) schedule NIC firmware update + reboot, 3) run full ECC memtest + stress for 2 hours, 4) if still failing -> schedule replacement. Anyone object?

rachel (platform): Cost note: replacements this quarter will hit capex/spare pool. If we can mitigate with firmware + memtest and keep SLAs, prefer deferring replacements to next cycle. But if we see repeated Xid after FW+memtest -> replace.

kevin (runtime): I'll attach the full logs to INF-4521 and tag @oncall for eu-west1. Also adding a short alert rule: if Xid13 per-card > 2 in 1h -> auto-softdrain.

maria (sre): +1. Also add a quick checksum: correlate tenant workload hashes to the Xid events to see if a specific model or client disproportionately triggers it. Could be opcode-specific.

toni (infra): good call. I'll run correlation job: 

```
./tools/xid_correlate --events /var/log/nv/xid_dump.log --query "batch_size<=2" --output xid_correlation.csv
```

ops-bot: [ticket INF-4521] created and assigned to eng-infra. Links: https://issues.redwood/c/INF-4521

maria (sre): OK team — let's follow the flow: sampling -> confirm -> softdrain -> firmware+memtest -> reassess 24h. If persistent, escalate for replacement.

toni (infra): Thanks — I'll post results here in ~40m. :hourglass:
